title: openai: /v1/chat.completions parity - params, roles, stop/logprobs, response formatting
author: Maya Gomez
release_notes: Add OpenAI /v1/chat.completions compatibility layer for params, roles, stop tokens, logprobs, and formatting. No breaking changes to Redwood API surface; enables a compat mode for third-party clients.
body: Motivation: customers and partner integrations expect near-drop-in compatibility with OpenAI's /v1/chat.completions semantics for parameters, role handling, stop tokens, and logprobs. This PR implements a compatibility layer and surface-level mappings while preserving Redwood's native API. Summary of changes: implement request param mapping (temperature, top_p, frequency_penalty, presence_penalty, max_tokens, n), enforce role normalization and delta streaming behavior, add stop token handling and fallback behavior, wire up logprobs request to engine-level scoring where available, and stabilize streaming response formatting to match OpenAI's event sequence for chat completions. Compatibility notes: the compat layer is opt-in via the header X-OpenAI-Compatible: true or by using the /openai/v1/chat.completions endpoint proxy; existing endpoints unchanged. Migration: SDKs updated to call new proxy endpoint when 'openai_compat' flag is enabled. Testing: added unit tests for param mapping and role normalization, E2E tests for streaming sequences and function/tool call structured output, and integration smoke tests against the runtime on both GPU and CPU configs. Rollout: staged canary behind feature flag, 50% traffic to compat proxy for first 24 hours, automatic rollback if 5xx rate or latency spike observed. Related tickets: ENG-4128 (compat spec), ENG-4139 (streaming stability), SUP-1182 (customer request).
commits_summary: 1) Implement openai compat proxy and request translator; 2) Role normalization and stop token handler; 3) Wire logprobs to scorer pipeline; 4) Streaming formatter to emit delta events matching OpenAI order; 5) Tests + docs + SDK examples; 6) Fixes from review: backpressure tweak, additional unit tests, logging improvements.
files_changed: redwood/pkg/openai_compat/proxy.go; redwood/pkg/openai_compat/translator.go; redwood/pkg/openai_compat/stream_formatter.go; redwood/runtime/streaming/streamer.go (stability/backpressure patch); redwood/sdk-python/redwood/openai_compat.py; redwood/sdk-ts/src/openaiCompat.ts; docs/openai_compat.md; test/e2e/openai_compat_streaming.test.ts; test/unit/openai_translator_test.go
review_comments: Eliot Chen: Please ensure role normalization preserves user-assigned names for assistant messages. Concern about mutating original Message objects; suggest copying before translation.
Maya Gomez: Addressed by making translator create deep copies and adding unit test to assert original is unchanged.
Priya Nair: Streaming order looks good but I saw duplicated delta tokens under high concurrency in canary. Recommend a small debounce on formatter flush and additional backpressure checks.
Maya Gomez: Added debounce of 5ms and tightened backpressure checks in streamer.go; included stress test that reproduces previous duplication and validates fix.
Marco Liu: Logprobs path looks fine but we should fallback gracefully when model does not expose token-level scores. Add doc entry describing when logprobs will be omitted.
Maya Gomez: Added fallback to null logprobs and documented behavior in docs/openai_compat.md.
QA - Anna Park: E2E streaming tests passed locally; saw intermittent 500s on first canary run but traced to an unrelated auth race which is being fixed separately (PR in flight).
merge_outcome: Merged after CI green and approvals from Eliot Chen and Priya Nair
guidance: Operational: enable feature flag openai_compat progressively. Observe metrics: per-route latency, 5xx rate, delta-event reorder rate, and CPU/GPU token throughput. SDK: use openai_compat helper in SDKs for request translation; no changes required for customers using Redwood native endpoints.
